1: At Jetavana, Venerable Dabba Mallaputta served as the Saṅgha’s steward, handing out meal tickets to the monks each morning.
2:
On days he got poor food, Venerable Lāludāyī threw the ticket hall into disorder:
“Does only Dabba know how to give out tickets, and not we?”
3: The monks said, “Then do it yourself,” and gave him the ticket basket. From then on Lāludāyī was the steward.
4: But he could not tell good rice from poor, nor did he know the order of seniority among the monks.
5: He scratched marks on the wall and ground to show where each group stood, and kept to them though the numbers changed every day.
6: When the monks tried to correct him, he would not listen: “I trust only my own marks.”
7: At last the young monks and novices pushed him out, saying he was unfit for the task, and there was a great uproar.
8: Hearing the noise, the Buddha asked Ānanda what was happening, and said that Lāludāyī had done the same in the past.
9: Long ago in Bārāṇasī the Bodhisatta was the king’s valuer. He priced elephants, horses and jewels fairly and paid their owners.
10: The greedy king thought, “This man will soon empty my treasury.”
11:
Looking out of his window, the king saw a foolish, greedy countryman
crossing the palace courtyard and called him in.
12: The king made that man his new valuer.
13: He set prices as he pleased, without regard to true worth, yet because of his office his word was final.
14: Then a horse-dealer came from the north with five hundred horses.
15: The foolish valuer priced all five hundred horses at a single measure of rice, and that was all the dealer received.
16: The dealer went to the Bodhisatta, the former valuer, who told him to bribe the fool and have him state the value of a measure of rice before the king.
17: The dealer bribed the foolish valuer and asked him to do so.
18:
Before the king, the dealer said,
“I accept the price of the horses, but please ask what a measure of rice is worth.”
19:
The foolish valuer declared,
“This measure of rice is worth all of Bārāṇasī, inside and outside the walls.”
20:
The ministers clapped and laughed: “So this great kingdom of Bārāṇasī, king and all,
is worth a measure of rice! What wisdom our valuer has!”
21:
The ministers mocked the king in a verse:
“What is a measure of rice worth? All of Bārāṇasī, inside and out, is worth one measure of rice!”
22: Ashamed, the king drove out the foolish valuer and gave the office back to the Bodhisatta.
23: “The foolish valuer then was Lāludāyī, and the wise valuer was I myself.”
